---
title: "Genetic augmentation of a clinical risk model for invasive mould disease"
subtitle: "A simulation study of incremental value: data report"
date: today
---

## The question

A validated clinical score (Stanzani et al., *J Infect* 2019) already predicts 60-day invasive mould disease
(IMD) in haematological inpatients with an aROC of 0.85. Candidate host variants in *PTX3*, *CLEC7A*
(dectin-1), *CD209* (DC-SIGN), *TLR4* and other genes are repeatedly reported as associated with invasive
aspergillosis. This project asks whether adding them to the score would change what a clinician does.

It is framed as a value-of-information question rather than a prediction-improvement exercise:

> Under what combinations of effect size, risk-allele frequency and linkage structure would host genetic
> information change clinical decisions for invasive mould disease in haematological patients, and is the
> published evidence anywhere near those combinations?

A negative answer, that no realistic genetic architecture moves the decision curve, is a finding and not a
failure. The primary endpoint is decision-curve net benefit at the 5% threshold, judged against a minimum
clinically important difference fixed before any genetic result exists.

::: {.callout-warning}
## This is a working report on provisional data

All extracted variant rows are marked `PENDING ROUND 2 VERIFICATION`. The correlation structure of the
clinical predictors is a fitted modelling assumption, not published data. No genetic result exists yet.
:::

## Where the project stands

| Phase | State |
|---|---|
| 0 Set-up | complete |
| 1 Literature search | complete: 831 unique records screened |
| 2 Screening and extraction | round 1 complete including targeted recovery and supplementary files; round 2 (human verification) not started |
| 3 Parameter derivation | design decisions settled; parameter derivation gated on round 2 |
| 4 Baseline reproduction | baseline coded and tested; baseline cohort is the observed distribution of the clinical profiles (D8), with the fitted copula as a sensitivity analysis; exact decision curves and MCID re-derived; patient link from Bologna outstanding |
| 5 Genetic layer simulation | blocked on phase 3 |
| 6 Sensitivity and architecture sweep | blocked on phase 5 |
| 7 Write-up | not started |
